The Chief Executive’s Report is presented to elected members at each SDCC monthly 
meeting. It forms a key part of our governance and oversight framework, supporting 
members in their role by providing timely updates on the work of the Council.
In line with Section 136(2) of the Local Government Act 2001 (as amended by the Local 
Government Reform Act 2014), the report outlines the performance of executive functions, 
the implementation of Council policy, and the delivery of services across the organisation.
This report should be read alongside updates provided to Area Committee Meetings and the 
quarterly Capital Progress Report, which together offer a comprehensive view of Council 
activity and progress.
Each edition includes:
•	Updates on how we are delivering on our Corporate Plan goals
•	Highlights of major initiatives and events
•	A visual snapshot of recent community and Council activities
The report also provides an opportunity to shine a light on areas of our work that may not 
always be in the spotlight but are vital to the day-to-day life of the county.

Climate Leadership
Environmental awareness initiatives and circular economy event 
Our Environmental Awareness team 
is progressing a number of initiatives 
to promote sustainable environmental 
practices, cleaner communities and 
greater awareness of 
Ireland’s transition to a circular 
economy. These include the Gum Litter 
Education Campaign, delivered in 
partnership with the Gum Litter Task 
Force, and the Anti-Litter Poster 
Competition displayed on Big Belly 
Solar Bins. Together, these activities 
help to encourage local environmental 
responsibility, support improved waste 
prevention and management and 
strengthen public consciousness of 
sustainability. 
As part of this work SDCC will host a 
free public Circular Economy event 
on 19 August in Fettercairn Community 
and Youth Centre. This will provide a 
community-based opportunity to share 
knowledge on waste prevention, reuse 
and sustainability. The event will include 
repair cafés for household items, a 
clothing swap and a plant exchange. 
These activities are designed to support 
waste prevention by keeping items in use 
for longer through repair, sharing and 
reuse.
 
Participants are invited to bring bicycles, 
furniture, clothing and household 
electrical and electronic items for repair 
guidance. Experts from the Rediscovery 
Centre and TOG Hackerspace will 
provide support in textiles, 
furniture, electronics and bicycles, with a 
focus on repair, restoration, redesign and 
upcycling.
If you want to refresh your wardrobe 
and save money while reducing textile 
waste, then bring your clothing items 
where they can be swapped for “new-to-
you” clean garments. For every item you 
bring you get a token to shop the rails 
for some fabulous finds to add to your 
wardrobe.   
A community plant swap will also take 
place providing participants with an 
opportunity to exchange indoor and 
outdoor plants, cuttings, seeds and 
gardening books while supporting 
local engagement on biodiversity and 
sustainable gardening. 
Save the date for this circular economy 
event and keep an eye on our social 
media for further updates.
Roll-out of public EV charging stations begins
We are working with our regional EV 
provider to deliver fast EV charging 
facilities across Dublin, making it easier 
for residents and visitors to charge their 
vehicles while using local services and 
amenities.  15 sites have been identified 
in our car parks, parks, libraries, district 
centres and leisure facilities as part 
of this rollout of new EV charging 
infrastructure. 
Electricity connection agreements 
are progressing, with connection offers 
secured for 11 sites and installations 
have now been completed at several 
locations, including Tandy’s Lane, 
Adamstown Park, Dodder Valley Park 
(R114), Dodder Valley Old Bawn 
Pavilions and Corkagh Park. These 
locations are awaiting final energisation 
by ESB and are 
expected to open for public use after 
this month. 
Further locations will be delivered as the 
programme rollout continues. All sites 
are being developed with accessibility 
considerations, supporting a more 
inclusive approach to EV charging 
infrastructure and cleaner transport.

Funding totalling €1,202,599 has been 
awarded for 27 projects under Phase 
2 of the Community Climate Action 
Programme. 
The funding will support a broad range 
of local community organisations 
to deliver practical climate action 
projects. Supported organisations 
include addiction services, social 
enterprises involved in local food 
growing, community centres, sports 
clubs and women’s collectives, 
reflecting the important role of local 
groups in advancing climate action at 
community level. Representatives of 
the organisations attended County 
Hall on 3 July, to mark their successful 
funding applications with our Climate 
Action team also providing guidance and 
support for project delivery. 
The programme is funded by the 
Department of Climate, Energy and the 
Environment and builds on Phase 1, 
through which 26 community projects 
delivered climate actions valued at over 
€1.1 million. These community-led 
projects make an important contribution 
to delivery of our Climate Action Plan 
and progress towards 2030 climate 
targets. 
More information on our Community 
Climate Action Programme is available at 
www.sdcc.ie
Over €1.2 million allocated to community climate action
Climate Leadership
Our Waste Enforcement and Licensing 
team has secured funding from the 
Department of Climate, Energy and 
the Environment under the 2026 Anti-
Dumping Initiative. This funding will 
support the delivery of several targeted 
programmes to address illegal dumping 
and support cleaner communities. A 
mattress amnesty which will operate 
from July to September will provide 
householders with an opportunity to 
recycle mattresses free of charge, 
while complimentary recycling of waste 
electrical and electronic equipment will 
also be available to help householders 
dispose of unwanted items safely and 
responsibly. 
The funding will also support temporary 
CCTV monitoring in a selected remote 
location which will assist in the 
prevention and detection of fly-tipping, 
support enforcement activity and 
contribute to the protection of the local 
environment. 
A dedicated clean-up project will also be 
undertaken in an area west of Clondalkin 
which has experienced repeated illegal 
dumping. The objective of this project 
is to restore the site and improve its 
condition for the benefit of the local 
community. 
Details of dates and locations for the 
mattress amnesty will be announced 
on www.sdcc.ie and through our social 
media.

The Pollinator Action Plan was launched 
by then Mayor Cllr Pamela Kearns on 18 
May. The plan reaffirms our commitment 
to embedding biodiversity and pollinator 
protection in the management of public 
lands. 
The plan which runs until 2030, builds on 
several years of progress and sets out a 
programme of action to support pollinators 
while enhancing the quality, resilience and 
enjoyment of public spaces. Our 
management of parks, open spaces and 
road verges has significantly evolved and 
been enhanced by our alignment with the 
All-Ireland Pollinator Plan. 
Approximately 210 hectares of meadows 
are now actively managed throughout 
South Dublin, significantly exceeding 
our original projections. These meadows 
are managed through ecological cutting 
schedules, allowing native wildflowers to 
bloom and set seed and improving food 
sources and nesting habitats for bees, 
butterflies, hoverflies and other pollinators 
with ongoing surveys showing year-on-year 
improvements in biodiversity.  
Our pollinator-friendly actions extend 
beyond meadow management: 
•	Since 2017, all parks, playgrounds and 
public gardens have been glyphosate-
free, with chemical use reduced across 
our operations. 
•	More than 7.5 million pollinator-friendly 
bulbs have been planted across over 90 
locations. 
•	We have mapped 1,720 kilometres of 
hedgerows, with over 400 kilometres 
actively managed as ecological corridors 
on our lands. 
New Pollinator Action Plan launched
Climate Leadership
•	A hedgerow restoration programme is 
being rolled out following successful 
local trials. 
•	In parallel, the mini woodland programme 
has delivered over 44,000 native 
trees in partnership with schools and 
communities. 
These measures are also delivering 
climate benefits, with reduced mowing 
practices estimated to prevent 116 
tonnes of CO2 emissions each year.   The 
Pollinator Action Plan sets out 30 targeted 
actions to be delivered by 2030, with 
the objective of embedding pollinator-
friendly principles across planning, design, 
capital projects and day-to-day operations. 
The plan also includes a strong emphasis 
on public engagement and shared 
ownership. Actions such as pollinator 
signage, online resources, park ranger-
led walks and communications activity 
support public understanding of visible 
management changes, including reduced 
mowing. National recognition through 
Pollinator Awards for Tymon Park 
and Waterstown Park further reflects the 
quality and consistency of the 
Council’s approach.  
The Pollinator Action Plan represents a 
practical commitment to protecting 
biodiversity, improving habitat quality and 
strengthening ecological connectivity 
across local communities. It supports 
a long-term vision for a connected and 
resilient county where pollinator- and 
biodiversity-friendly habitats 
support nature, strengthen climate 
resilience and enhance quality of life 
for residents, businesses and visitors.   See 
the full plan online at www.sdcc.ie.

Quality Housing
€17.5 million funding for infrastructure at Killinarden Foothills
Funding totalling €17.5 million has 
been secured under the first phase of 
the Housing Infrastructure Investment 
Fund programme to support the delivery 
of new homes at Killinarden Foothills. 
This significant allocation forms part 
of a multi-annual national investment 
strategy aimed at unlocking serviced 
land and accelerating housing delivery at 
scale. 
The funding will enable the provision 
of critical infrastructure to support 
the Killinarden Foothills residential 
and community scheme, which will 
deliver approximately 635 new homes, 
alongside a new community facility, 
high-quality public realm, and a strategic 
spine road. The development will provide 
a balanced tenure mix of affordable, 
social and private housing, directly 
addressing identified housing demand 
within the county. 
Phase 1 infrastructure works are already 
underway, with the delivery of the 
community centre, playing pitches, and 
a substantial portion of the public realm 
expected to be completed next year. 
This investment marks a key milestone 
in our continued commitment to 
achieving both national and local housing 
objectives. By enabling the delivery of a 
significant number of homes on serviced 
lands, the project will make a meaningful 
contribution to regional and national 
housing supply targets while supporting 
sustainable urban growth. 
A central benefit of the infrastructure 
works is the integration of the 
new development with existing 
neighbourhoods. The scheme will 
include connected street networks, 
enhanced pedestrian and cycle 
permeability, and coordinated open 
space provision. These elements 
will ensure that the development 
complements and strengthens the 
surrounding urban structure, promotes 
active travel, improves accessibility, and 
contributes to the enhancement of the 
wider Killinarden area. 
Overall, the Killinarden Foothills project 
represents a strategic investment in 
housing and community infrastructure, 
combining substantial residential 
delivery with long-term social and 
economic benefits. The HIIF funding is 
critical to enabling the development of 
a well-connected, tenure-balanced and 
high-quality neighbourhood, delivering 
lasting value for both current and future 
residents.

Quality Housing
Mayor officially opens Swiftbanks housing development in Saggart
The official opening of Swiftbanks in 
Saggart marked an important milestone 
in the delivery of new homes in South 
Dublin County, with the development 
providing a significant mix of social, cost 
rental and affordable purchase homes 
for individuals, first-time buyers and 
families. 
The opening was attended by new 
Mayor, Cllr. Francis Timmons, elected 
members, Chief Executive Colm Ward, 
representatives of Tuath Housing and 
Cairn Homes, as well as new residents 
of the development, along with 
staff, contractors, design teams and 
community stakeholders involved in 
bringing the development to completion. 
Swiftbanks sees 264 new homes 
provided, including 143 social homes, 
95 cost rental homes and 26 affordable 
purchase homes. The affordable 
purchase homes comprises a range of 
three-bedroom homes made available 
by under the Affordable Dwelling 
Purchase Agreement, supporting eligible 
purchasers, including first-time buyers, 
to access home ownership. 
The development provides high-quality, 
energy-efficient homes in a growing 
community, with a focus on modern 
design, comfort and sustainability. The 
homes are designed to support long-
term, secure living and to enable new 
residents to put down roots in the wider 
Saggart area. 
The project is a strong example of 
housing delivery through partnership, 
involving SDCC, Tuath Housing and 
Cairn Homes, with support from central 
government funding. This collaborative 
approach has enabled the delivery 
of homes across a range of tenures, 
responding to local housing needs. 
Speaking at the opening, the Mayor 
described Swiftbanks as “a clear 
example of how ambition, planning and 
partnership can translate into real homes 
and real opportunities for people in 
South Dublin”. 
Swiftbanks represents another positive 
step forward in addressing housing need 
in South Dublin and demonstrates our 
continued commitment to delivering 
homes, supporting sustainable 
communities and working with partners 
to achieve tangible outcomes for 
residents.

Quality Housing
Our new Tenant Participation Strategy was 
officially launched at Balgaddy Community 
Centre on 10 June with local residents 
along with pupils from Devine Mercy 
Senior National School in attendance. The 
strategy runs from 2025 to 2029 and 
sets out our commitment to ensuring that 
South Dublin remains an inclusive, safe 
and welcoming place to live, work and 
visit. With responsibility for managing over 
10,500 social homes, we aim to empower 
tenants by promoting, encouraging 
and supporting active engagement, 
strengthening civic pride, and fostering 
a greater sense of connection and 
belonging within local communities. 
Tenant participation is a two-way process 
in which tenants work in partnership with 
the council to share ideas, exchange 
information and contribute to decisions 
that improve housing services. 
Through the strategy, we will continue 
to listen to tenants and work with them 
to identify practical ways to support and 
improve quality of life in the places where 
they live. As a citizen-centred organisation, 
we recognise that meaningful tenant 
participation is central to improving 
social housing services and building 
Balgaddy pilot to lead new tenant participation approach
inclusive, active and safe communities. 
This approach supports better decision-
making, strengthens relationships with 
communities and partners, and helps 
lay the foundations for a resilient and 
sustainable future for local communities. 
Our dedicated Estate Management team 
works to support tenants and manage 
our tenancies.  Our Housing Officers 
will support the establishment of locally 
based tenant participation working groups 
within estates, ensuring tenants have 
opportunities to share ideas, provide 
feedback and contribute to service 
improvements in their communities. We 
will also promote cross-departmental 
co-operation to support local initiatives 
such as Tidy Towns through community 
supports, funding and training, and will 
continue to actively engage and inform 
communities on climate action initiatives. 
Building on recent development work 
in Balgaddy, the area has been selected 
as the pilot location for the Tenant 
Participation Strategy. This structured 
pilot will support refinement and 
enhancement of our approaches to tenant 
engagement, identify practical supports 
and strengthen future implementation. 
By placing tenants’ voices at the centre 
of estate management and service 
improvement, the strategy will support 
stronger communities, better local 
outcomes and a more responsive service.

A Thriving Economy
Success for LEO South Dublin client at National Enterprise Awards  
Áine Kennedy of The Smooth Company, 
representing, LEO South Dublin was 
named Best Export Business at the 
National Enterprise Awards in The Mansion 
House, Dublin, on 18 June, following her 
success n at the Local Enterprise Awards 
South Dublin in March.  
Since launching the business from her attic 
in 2022, with her Grandad Billy helping to 
pack orders, Áine has grown The Smooth 
Company into a global beauty brand loved 
in over 90 countries and supported by a 
team of seven employees. 
The Smooth Stick has not only become 
a fan favourite but has also become an 
internet sensation, with over 150 million 
views on TikTok plus the introduction of 5 
more products - the 4 in 1 Smooth Styler 
Comb, The Dapper Stick️ (a surprise 
collaboration with Grandad Billy!), the 
viral Mane Master smoothing brush, the 
Smoothing Travel Brush and Smooth 
Dream 11 in 1 Hair Styling Cream. 
Áine was named as one of the Sunday 
Independent 30 under 30 Irish 
businesspeople to watch. She is also the 
winner of an Emerging New Business 
Award by the Small Firms Association, 
winner of the ‘Young Entrepreneur Of 
The Year’ at the Irish Woman Of The Year 
awards 2023 and most recently, won 
Image PWC Young Businesswoman of 
the Year Award in 2024. 
Local Enterprise Office clients transition to Enterprise Ireland 
We are delighted to announce that the 
following clients have recently progressed 
to Enterprise Ireland, marking an important 
milestone in their business growth. 
Supported through LEO South Dublin’s 
financial assistance, training and mentoring, 
these businesses have developed the 
capacity and ambition to move to the next 
stage of their enterprise journey. 
The Smooth Company 
Founded in 2022, The Smooth Company 
is a global brand known for its innovative 
haircare products in 90+ countries around 
the world. The company’s flagship product 
is the Smooth Stick™, the brand has 
expanded its product range to include 10 
viral hair smoothing products and tools, and 
it is stocked in major retailers like Brown 
Thomas, Arnotts, and Cloud 10 Beauty, as 
well as on their online store. Founder Áine 
Kennedy and The Smooth Company have 
earned significant recognition, receiving a 
range of prestigious awards at both national 
and international level such as Best Irish 
Beauty Brand at the VIP Awards and named 
EY Emerging Entrepreneur of the Year in 
2025. 
My Cloud PA 
My Cloud PA is an integrated platform 
established in 2021. The company 
specialises in digitalisation services, 
offering tools for customer relationship 
management (CRM), financial management, 
e-commerce and digital marketing. My 
Cloud PA was shortlisted for the 2023 
National Startup Awards in the Tech 
Startup category, marking a significant 
milestone and national recognition of the 
company’s innovation and growth. 
Covy Watersport 
Established in 2023, Covy Watersport Ltd 
design elite, athlete tested performance 
sailing wear, developed through direct 
collaboration with Ireland’s Olympic and 
international sailors. Covy is Ireland’s 
first ever sailing brand and is the official 
kit supplier to both Irish Sailing and the 
Northern Ireland Sailing Team from 2026 
onwards. 
Decision Analytics  
Decision Analytics is a data and AI 
company specialising in business 
intelligence, analytics, and digital 
transformation solutions. Founded in 
2022, the company helps organisations 
unlock the full value of their data by 
integrating disparate systems into a 
single, reliable source of truth and 
delivering real time insights to support 
faster, smarter decision making. A key 
part of the company’s offering is its 
proprietary platform, including tools such 
as ChimeHive, designed to improve time 
tracking, job costing, and operational 
efficiency on the shop floor. Decision 
Analytics was named a 2025 winner at the 
European CEO of the Year Awards, hosted 
by EU Business News.

A Thriving Economy
12th Lock multimedia studio moves to construction phase
A significant milestone has been reached 
in the delivery of the 12th Lock multimedia 
Studio, with the construction contract now 
signed and works expected to begin in the 
coming weeks. 
Vision Contracting has been appointed 
as the contractor for the project, which 
received planning permission in July 2024. 
The new facility is being developed as part 
of the wider 12th Lock Masterplan and 
is designed to support the growth of the 
creative industries. The studio will provide 
dedicated spaces for film and television 
production, digital content creation, 
podcasting, gaming and visual effects, 
alongside exhibition areas, workshops, 
creative offices, co‑working spaces and 
informal social areas. 
The project forms part of a broader vision 
for the 12th Lock area that seeks to create 
a vibrant destination with high‑quality 
public spaces that complement the natural 
setting. Investment has been allocated 
through the Capital Programme to support 
delivery of the studio and other elements 
of the masterplan. When completed, the 
facility will be operated by 12th Lock 
Creative Industries under the leadership 
of Oscar‑nominated producer Gary 
Levinsohn. The studio is intended to 
provide opportunities for collaboration, 
innovation and skills development within 
the creative sector, supporting emerging 
and established talent. 
The development complements other 
strategic initiatives being advanced in 
partnership with Lens Media, including 
the proposed Dublin Fields media 
campus at Grange Castle. Together, 
these projects aim to strengthen the 
region’s position as a leading location for 
film, television, digital media and creative 
production. 
Construction is expected to continue into 
2027, with the facility scheduled to open 
next year.
“Love Lucan” initiate launched to support local businesses
The launch of the Love Lucan campaign 
marks a significant and exciting new 
chapter for Lucan village following the 
extensive public realm enhancement 
works in the area. These upgrades have 
transformed the heart of the village, 
creating a more attractive and vibrant 
space for residents, businesses and 
visitors alike. Now, with the physical 
improvements in place, the focus turns 
to showcasing everything that makes 
Lucan a unique and thriving destination.  
At its core, the Love Lucan campaign 
is about celebrating local pride and 
promoting the diverse offering within 
the village. It is a collaborative campaign 
between SDCC and local businesses 
running from 29 June to 30 August. 
Through a coordinated use of social 
media, striking photography and 
engaging video content, the campaign 
aims to highlight Lucan’s rich blend 
of heritage, hospitality, retail and 
community spirit. From its picturesque 
streets and historical landmarks to its 
bustling cafés, shop and services, Lucan 
has so much to offer and the campaign 
seeks to bring these stories to life in a 
modern and dynamic way.  
Local businesses are at the heart of 
this initiative. They have been actively 
encouraged to participate by sharing 
their own content, promoting their 
products and services and contributing 
to a wider, unified message about the 
village. This collaborative approach 
not only strengthens the visibility of 
individual businesses but also builds 
a stronger collective identity for 
Lucan as a destination. By working 
together under the Love Lucan banner, 
businesses can amplify their reach and 
engage new audiences both locally and 
beyond. 
In addition to its economic benefits, 
the campaign plays an important role 
in fostering community pride. It invites 
residents to rediscover their local 
area and to become ambassadors for 
Lucan by sharing their own experiences 
and favourite spots. In doing so, it 
strengthens the connection between 
people and place, reinforcing a sense of 
belonging and shared identity. 
The launch of Love Lucan represents 
a timely and forward-looking initiative. 
With the enhanced public realm 
providing an attractive and welcoming 
backdrop, the campaign ensures that 
Lucan’s renewed energy is visible to all. 
By raising awareness and generating 
interest through online platforms, 
Love Lucan seeks to encourage more 
people to visit, explore and experience 
everything the area has to offer by 
highlighting the many reasons to 
choose Lucan as a place to spend time.

Expressions of interest are invited 
from community and local partnership 
groups for the Outdoor Recreation 
Infrastructure Scheme (ORIS) 
2026/2027. The scheme is administered 
by the council and funded by the 
Department of Rural and Community 
Development and the Gaeltacht.  
The scheme supports the 
development and maintenance of 
outdoor recreation infrastructure for 
activities including walking, canoeing, 
mountain biking, orienteering and wild 
swimming. 
Projects should generally be located 
in rural areas, and the scheme 
can also support recreational 
infrastructure that links towns or 
villages to significant outdoor recreation 
facilities in the countryside, as well 
as amenities located near rivers or lakes 
and water-based projects within town 
environs.
Expressions of interest for the Project 
Development Measure and Measure 1 
must be submitted by Friday 17 July 
2026. Applications for Measure 2 and 
Measure 3 must be submitted by Friday 
14 August 2026. Community and local 
partnership groups are encouraged 
to submit proposals in advance of the 
relevant closing date to allow sufficient 
time for review and processing.
Further information and expression of 
interest forms are available at www.sdcc.
ie.

Expressions of interest invited for ORIS
We are currently progressing sustainable 
transport improvements on Belgard 
Road between the Old Blessington 
Road junction and the Cookstown 
Road junction, in conjunction with the 
National Transport Authority (NTA). 
This forms Phase 1 of the Tallaght to 
Clondalkin Active Travel Scheme. The 
proposed improvements are a key 
element of Cycle South Dublin and form 
part of Route No. 4, linking Tallaght to 
Clondalkin.  
The scheme is being progressed under 
Section 38 of the Road Traffic Act 
1994, following public consultation. The 
contract has been awarded to Clonmel 
Enterprises Ltd., with works scheduled 
to commence in August. 
The project will provide wider and 
safer cycle lanes on Belgard Road from 
Old Blessington Road to Cookstown 
Road. The cycle lanes will be segregated 
from traffic by a raised concrete 
kerb. Existing narrow cycle lanes will be 
widened into the grass verge to a width 
of 2 metres, with traffic lanes narrowed 
to 3 metres in some locations.  
The project also includes the 
following measures:  
•	Improvement to junctions along the 
route to provide safe crossings and 
connections for all road users.  
•	An upgrade of the Airton Road/Belgard 
Road junction to provide protected 
cycle facilities in accordance with the 
Cycle Design Manual   
•	Safe crossing facilities for pedestrians 
and cyclists on all four arms of the 
roundabout at Belgard Road/Belgard 
Square North.  
The image below provides an overview 
of the proposed improvements between 
the Old Blessington Road and Belgard 
Square North junctions with Belgard 
Road.

Urban Speed Limit Review – consultation and implementation
A Better Place
St. Cuthberts Park enhancement works nearing completion
The Urban Speed Limit Review 2026–
2027 is a key road safety initiative aimed 
at creating safer roads and streets within 
our local communities. The review forms 
part of a national programme focused on 
reducing road casualties and improving 
conditions for vulnerable road users, 
including pedestrians and cyclists. 
The review is assessing existing speed 
limits across urban areas, with a clear 
emphasis on aligning limits with the 
function and character of each road. 
Evidence demonstrates that lower 
vehicle speeds significantly reduce both 
the likelihood and severity of collisions. 
Accordingly, the programme seeks to 
deliver self-explaining, context driven 
speed limits that are credible, consistent 
and easier to enforce. 
Typical outcomes of the review may 
include: 
•	30 km/h speed limits in residential 
areas, town centres and around schools, 
supporting road safety and place-
making objectives; 
•	50 km/h limits on distributor and link 
roads where appropriate; 
•	60 km/h limits on arterial routes 
with suitable design standards and 
separation from vulnerable road users. 
A particular focus of the review will be 
school zones, where periodic 30 km/h 
speed limits may be introduced during 
school operating hours through electronic 
signage to enhance safety for children 
and families. 
The programme is being delivered in 
accordance with the Road Traffic Act 
2004 and national speed management 
guidance, with key milestones established 
for consultation, statutory processes 
and implementation. The Special Speed 
Limit Bye-Law process is scheduled 
to conclude by October 2026, with 
implementation of approved speed limits, 
associated signage and mapping updates 
to be completed by March next year. 
Engagement is central to the review 
process. Draft proposals are first 
being brought to Elected Members at 
Electoral Area level, before progressing 
to public consultation. This will give 
local communities and key stakeholders, 
including An Garda Síochána, the 
National Transport Authority, Transport 
Infrastructure Ireland and neighbouring 
local authorities, the opportunity to take 
part and make submissions. 
The adoption of revised speed limits 
later this year will support our wider 
road safety, active travel and sustainable 
transport objectives, contributing to safer 
communities and improved quality of life 
across South Dublin. 
Enhancement works at St Cuthbert’s 
Park, Clondalkin recommenced in May 
2026 with vegetation removal around 
the 12th century church ruin. The €2.2 
million investment in the 12-hectare 
park area will provide an enhanced 
outdoor amenity for the local community, 
including two playspaces, a teenspace, a 
3x3 basketball court, a multi-use games 
area, new footpaths and cycle routes, 
lighting and drainage upgrades to existing 
pitches. 
The works are scheduled for completion 
later this month and an exciting 
programme of family-focused events 
is planned for the summer months 
to mark the completion of the project.  
We acknowledge the patience and 
co-operation of the local community 
throughout the delivery of these works.

Launch of new Road Safety Strategy 
A Better Place
Our new Road Safety Strategy has 
been launched in a key step towards 
achieving Vision Zero. The strategy sets 
out a clear plan for safer local roads 
and aligns closely with the Government 
Road Safety Strategy. It will be delivered 
with a heightened focus on the provision 
of improved infrastructure, road user 
behaviour, education, and enforcement. 
The starting point is recognising that 
road deaths or serious injuries should not 
be the price to pay for our mobility. Our 
aim is to be a place where it is safe for 
all road users to travel to and from their 
destination safely, acknowledging the 
devasting human cost of road trauma on 
our roads and the lifelong impact it has 
on those who have lost loved ones.  
We will deliver this through the Safe 
System approach, recognizing that while 
people make mistakes, our transport 
network must be designed and managed, 
so those errors never result in death 
or life-changing injuries. Collaboration 
from all stakeholders is key to achieving 
this and we work closely with our ‘Road 
Safety Working Together Group’ to 
achieve this.

Clondalkin village enhancement commencement

Framework (LPF) was approved by 
Council in March 2026. Section 8.6 of 
the LPF provides the concept design for 
a future village enhancement. 
The objective of village enhancement 
will be to improve the functionality, 
aesthetic and accessibility of the public 
realm for all age groups and abilities. 
Further aims of the project will be to 
deliver additional greening, biodiversity 
and sustainability that will invite and 
encourage the community to engage 
with the public spaces. 
As with all our local traditional villages,

Clondalkin, this is well reflected by

village.

Pride Week at SDCC 
Pride Week was marked by a programme 
of events focused on promoting 
awareness, inclusion and allyship among 
staff and the wider community. 
The week began with a Lunch and Learn 
session held in the county hall foyer on 22 
June. Delivered by Pride at Work Ireland, 
the session explored the theme “How 
to be an Ally.” Staff were encouraged 
to consider the importance of LGBTQ+ 
allyship both in the workplace and in 
everyday life. The session highlighted 
practical ways to demonstrate support, 
including participating in Pride events, 
using inclusive and respectful language, 
and actively challenging homophobia 
and transphobia. Participants were also 
invited to reflect on personal biases and 
build confidence in fostering an inclusive 
working environment. 
A staff coffee morning provided a further 
opportunity for engagement, enabling 
colleagues to meet members of the 
SDCC LGBTQ+ Staff Network and learn 
more about its role in supporting inclusion 
across the organisation. 
SDCC Libraries also played a central 
role in marking Pride Month, continuing 
their strong commitment to inclusivity, 
diversity and community engagement. 
A varied programme of events created 
opportunities for people of all ages to 
celebrate equality and explore LGBTQ+ 
culture and experiences. 
Throughout June, our libraries hosted 
a range of inclusive and accessible 
activities, including Pride bingo sessions, 
makerspace workshops and karaoke 
events. 
Film screenings exploring LGBTQ+ 
stories, alongside digital exhibitions on 
LGBTQ+ history and culture, provided 
both in-person and online opportunities 
for learning and engagement. 
A highlight of the programme was 
participation in the Dublin Pride parade 
on 27 June. Library staff, in a mobile 
library, took part in the parade for 
the fourth consecutive year, joining 
community groups, organisations and 
supporters from across the city in a 
vibrant and visible celebration of Pride.

dash took place on Saturday 27 June 
in Corkagh Park and once again proved 
to be an enjoyable day out for all. The 
event was sold out in advance, with 
almost 1,500 people attending on the 
day, ready to take part in the 2km route. 
Participants ran, walked or took the 
route at their own pace, getting covered 
in coloured powder along the way. The

family entertainment ran from 11.00am

setting of Corkagh Park. The Colour 
Dash continues to be one of the most 
popular events in the Active South 
Dublin programme, and this year was 
no different. With strong attendance, 
great energy and plenty of smiles, it was 
a brilliant way to celebrate the start of 
summer — full of colour, fun and good 
community spirit.

natural dyes, botanical prints and colourful

on planting and seed dispersal.

continuing development of The Garden

continue to grow over the summer months 
through community participation, creative 
collaboration, and environmental action

County Hall autism friendly accreditation 
Over the past year we have been working 
with AsIAm (Ireland’s autism charity) 
to achieve Autism-Friendly Service 
User Accreditation for county hall. We 
are pleased to report that we are now 
approaching the final stage of this 
process: the agreement of a Charter of 
Inclusion between SDCC and AsIAm. 
As an initial step, we partnered with 
AsIAm to carry out a comprehensive 
environmental audit of county hall. The 
findings from this audit informed the 
development of a sensory map and a 
visual guide to the building. In addition, 
dedicated visual guides have been 
created for the council chamber and our 
housing customer centre, to support 
visitors using these spaces. All resources 
are available at www.sdcc.ie  
To further support accessibility and 
inclusivity, AsIAm delivered three 
tailored training sessions to staff from 
a range of customer-facing roles. These 
sessions were designed to help staff 
better understand autism, including 
what it is and what it is not, while 
addressing common myths, strengths 
and misconceptions. They also explored 
autistic characteristics and supportive 
communication strategies to help staff 
provide a more inclusive service to 
autistic service users. 
 These initiatives represent a positive 
step towards creating a more inclusive 
and accessible environment for autistic 
service users in county hall.

New housing liaison service for survivors of Industrial and Reformatory 
schools 
A dedicated Housing Liaison Officer has 
been appointed to support survivors 
of industrial and reformatory schools 
in accessing local authority housing 
information, guidance and assistance. 
The service forms part of the wider 
Government commitment to recognise 
the experiences of survivors and ensure 
that housing needs are considered with 
compassion and sensitivity, including 
through prioritisation on compassionate 
grounds where appropriate. 
The role will provide as a clear and 
supportive point of contact for survivors 
and, where requested and with explicit 
consent, their advocate. The role is to 
help survivors understand available 
housing supports, navigate relevant 
processes and link with the appropriate 
Housing Department teams. 
Support may relate to social housing 
applications, transfers, homeless 
supports, rent and arrears, maintenance, 
private housing loans and grants, and 
Traveller accommodation services. 
The Liaison Officer will not make 
decisions on housing applications or 
services. The service will be delivered in 
a respectful, confidential and trauma-
informed manner, with survivors not 
required to relive their experiences. 
Where verification is needed, this will be 
approached as sensitively as possible. 
This important new service provides 
a dedicated pathway for survivors to 
engage with the council on housing 
matters in a way that is accessible, 
compassionate and practical.

Further public consultation on County Development Plan variation 
Proposed Variation No. 2 to the County 
Development Plan was considered at 
special meetings of the council on 19 
and 24 June after the Chief Executive’s 
Report was published in response to 
extensive public submissions made 
during the process. The proposed 
variation arises from the revised 
National Planning Framework (NPF) and 
associated Section 28 guidelines issued 
by the Department of Housing, Local 
Government and Heritage, which seek 
to ensure sufficient zoned land to meet 
projected population growth.  
Under revised targets, SDCC is 
required to accommodate an uplift of 
approximately 600 additional housing 
units per annum in addition to the 
current Development Plan provision and 
into the future to meet housing demand. 
This variation marks an important step 
in aligning the Development Plan with 
updated national planning policy.  
The special meeting of the council 
considered 180 motions including 
decisions on zoning lands and specific 
local objectives. Following consideration 
by the elected members, it was 
County Matters
resolved that modifications to the 
variation are required and that these 
constitute material alterations to the 
proposed variation. A further period of 
public consultation relating to material 
alterations commenced on 7 July.
The material alterations to the proposed 
variation will include proposals to 
add new lands for residential zoning 
at Cornerpark Newcastle, additional/
amended specific local objectives on 
new residential zonings at Ballynakelly 
Newcastle, Adamstown West, Tubber 
Lane, Edmonstown Road, Citywest, 
Liffey Valley Shopping Centre, 
Edmonstown Road and Foxhunter and 
to remove proposed residential zoning 
and specific local objectives on lands 
at St Edmundsbury, Finnstown Castle 
and Coldcut Road. Following public 
consultation and a Chief Executive 
report, decisions on the material 
alterations and a resolution on the 
proposed variation will be made at a 
council meeting later this year.

SDCC and IPB launch Local Environmental Action Fund
The Local Environmental Action Fund 
(LEAF) joint initiative between SDCC and 
IPB Insurance was officially launched by 
the Mayor of South Dublin, Cllr Francis 
Timmons in Rathfarnham Castle Park 
on Monday 6 July.  LEAF provides a 
€100,000 local fund available to Tidy 
Towns, Residents’ Associations and 
voluntary groups to support community-
led projects focused on Environmental 
Enhancement, Biodiversity and Climate 
Action.
The LEAF initiative is a coordinated 
national Communities Working 
Together for Climate fund and Mayor 
Timmons noted that “the joint initiative 
will provide the support to empower 
Tidy Towns members and voluntary 
Community Groups to deliver visible and 
practical environmental improvements 
in local areas. Whether your community 
wants to create a new green space, 
improve local biodiversity, boost energy 
efficiency, or reduce food waste, this 
fund is here to help.”
This initiative builds on the strength and 
legacy of the Tidy Towns movement 
and community volunteers, whose 
contributions play a key role in 
enhancing quality of life and supporting 
Ireland’s climate and biodiversity goals.
Graham Orr, Director of Member and 
Client Relations at IPB Insurance, 
highlighted the Fund’s importance 
within IPB’s Centenary Year saying, 
“As Ireland’s local government mutual 
insurer, IPB Insurance exists to protect 
County Matters
our members who, every day, serve 
the public and their communities. Our 
mutual ethos goes beyond insurance, 
it’s about giving back and supporting 
initiatives that strengthen communities 
and enhance places. In our centenary 
year, this Fund represents a meaningful 
investment in the future of towns and 
communities across Ireland, delivered 
in partnership with the local authorities 
who founded IPB. I am particularly 
delighted to see the fund launching here 
today in South Dublin”
Grants of €1,000 to €25,000 are 
available to fully finance high-impact 
local projects such as biodiversity, 
sustainability, water conservation, 
circular economy, renewable energy 
and waste reduction initiatives that will 
enhance the local environment. 
The applicant group must be a Tidy 
Towns or other voluntary group that 
undertakes similar activities such as 
a resident association. The proposed 
project must include collaboration 
with at least one other community 
stakeholder group including but not 
limited to local schools, scouts groups, 
youth clubs, sports clubs, women’s 
sheds, men’s sheds, community gardens.
Project examples include, but are not 
limited to:
•	Perennial planting aligned with the 
SDCC Pollinator Plan / All Ireland 
Pollinator Plan
•	Tree planting and urban greening 
initiatives e.g. planting on sports club 
grounds, schools
•	Renewable Energy Projects e.g. 
installing small solar systems e.g. 
Community Centres
•	Water Conservation e.g. waterbutts, 
rain-gardens, rainwater harvesting
•	Repair Café’s and waste reduction and 
recycling initiatives
•	Public education campaigns on 
sustainability
•	Climate resilience projects e.g. flood 
prevention measures
